value.hook: Open before adding a retry, backoff or reconnect to any daemon client (pij-rs, the pij router, OMP or Copilot extension), or diagnosing failures during a bounce
value.title: Retrying daemon calls across a restart: refused only, new key, abort to the end (F174, #219)

sections.name: body
sections.value:
F174 (#219, three review rounds) taught these. Each was a finding or a CI failure.

1. Retry only a refused connection. Nothing reached the daemon, so a write can't happen twice. A reset, a timeout or any reply is answered once: a reset is a request the daemon may have read. Prove it with a fake that reads the request and drops it, and assert it was sent once.
2. Every daemon boot mints a new bearer key and publishes it after it binds. A retry must re-read daemon.key before each try (key-file clients only, never a job token). One 401 right after a recovery is retryable with the key read again: require_bearer refuses before any handler runs. A 401 with no restart behind it is an answer. Fixtures that don't check Authorization hid this; make the replacement server validate the header and test both publication orders.
3. Plumb the tool call's abort signal through every request it makes, including follow-ups (pij_spawn's task send was round 3's block). Check the signal after each pause.
4. Decide per caller who waits. Person/tool calls (pij-rs verbs, pij_send, pij_spawn) wait about 20 s. Hooks, registration and inbox loops (which have their own backoff), ping (`just doctor` reads a failure as "not running"), whoami and commit-trailers answer at once. A blanket extension retry broke the Copilot registration test.
5. The pij router probes /health before a routed call and turns a refused probe into an immediate E-RS-UNPORTED, so a Rust-client retry never runs for `pij send <seat>`. The probe needs its own wait. Tests that run the real CLI against a closed port set PIJ_RS_RESTART_WAIT_MS=0.
6. Cap JS waits by wall clock as well as the summed sleep budget (ocelot).
7. "About a minute" was about a second. Read the records before believing a report: `log show` (mDNSResponder connection STOP/START by pid), `ps -o lstart=`, daemon.log's "listening on", and the seat's events.jsonl tool start and complete times. `just bounce-rs` kills with SIGTERM, so in-flight requests get a reset; `pij daemon bounce` sends SIGINT and drains.
8. With no local build, round 1's first push failed CI: my helper `send` clashed with DaemonClient's public `send`. Grep the type for a new method's name before pushing blind.
